title: Generational Wealth
hook: Making money is one skill. Keeping it for decades is a completely different one.
statement: Wealth has to survive time, not just get created. Growth only counts after you subtract the losses.
explainer: Debt, bad calls, no plan for what happens next. Losses quietly eat your growth. If you lose almost as fast as you grow, nothing gets passed on.
sop: List your assets: property, investments, business equity, retirement.
List what could erode them: debt, no estate plan, no diversification.
Estimate your yearly Growth % and Loss % honestly.
Reinvest one income stream into an owned, appreciating asset.
Set up a basic protection plan this quarter: will, beneficiaries, diversification.
equation_example: Growth 8% a year minus Loss 3% a year = 5% net. Higher means wealth compounds across years and generations. Falling or negative means it's eroding faster than you build it, no matter your income.
question: Write down the biggest thing quietly eroding your wealth right now.
closing_statement: Build wealth that survives you, not just supports you.
caption:
Principle Nº 181: Generational Wealth
